newsitem.title: USA: Luxottica drops after Merrill downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Luxottica drops after Merrill downgrade.

text.p: Shares in Italian eyeglass maker Luxottica Group SpA fell sharply on Thursday following a downgrade by Merrill Lynch analyst Deepak Raj.
Shares fell 6-3/4, or 10.4 percent, to 58 in late-afternoon trade. Volume was a heavy 102,700 shares.

"The market for frames, and sunglasses in particular, may have slower growth in the near term," Raj wrote in an analysis. He cut the company's shares to near-term accumulate from near-term neutral and kept them at long-term buy.

He said higher levels of retail inventory may harm sales for the next several quarters. "Despite weak economic conditions in core markets (e.g. Italy), Luxottica appears to be gaining market share and should have solid growth over the long term."
His earnings per share estimates are $2.96 to $3.00 and $3.40 to $3.50 in 1996 and 1997, respectively. Prior estimates were $3.00 to $3.05 and $3.55 to $3.60.
Asked why Luxottica shares were down, Bear Stearns analyst Constance Maneaty said, "There was a Merrill downgrade. That's the only reason."
